summary: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at the MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Moscow State University, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Gritli von Mitterwallner worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her Dr. phil. (1964) and habilitation (1971) at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He became an Assistant Professor at the University of Hong Kong around 2003 and visited UBC in 2007.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from 1986 to 2004, and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University around 2004.
Guankong worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and became a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima studied law at the University of Tokyo and trained under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. A Buddhist studies scholar, he lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute, and founded Dogen Sangha International in 2007.

Gudrun Bühnemann works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Münster, Bonn, and Vienna (under Ernst Steinkellner), held research posts in India and Japan, and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. By 2026, she held research posts at the Göttingen Academy, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Munich.
Gunapala Dharmasiri was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an attested academic post at the University of Ceylon in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and held a post at Uppsala University from around 1978 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from 1926 to 1933 and subsequently held a post there from 1933 to 1940.

Guo Jun works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Monash University, the University of Sydney, and Fuyan Buddhist Institute, he studied under Song Nian, Sheng Yen, and Qinyin, and served as abbot of Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Rissho University under Kenyu Mitomo and studied under Sheng Yen, Hoyo Watanabe, and other teachers.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Baring Union Christian College, Kent, Harvard, and Columbia, he taught at Columbia (1988–1999) and held the Sikh Studies Chair at UC Santa Barbara (1999–2015).

id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a religious studies scholar. After studying at Leiden University (1893–1901), he held posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, also studying with Hla Pe and John Okell, and later served as a Senior Teaching Fellow at SOAS.

Gustaf John Ramstedt specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (1893–1902) and later held posts at the University of Helsinki (1909–1941) and the University of Tokyo (1919–1929).

Gustav Haloun was a sinologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Vienna, Leipzig (under August Conrady), and Charles University. He held positions at Halle-Wittenberg and Göttingen before serving as Chair of Chinese at Cambridge from 1938 to 1951.

Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, Marburg (under Rudolf Otto), and Göttingen, later holding posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).
